channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias held above strong support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports EUR/USD holding near 1.1440 with a firmer underlying tone. The pair is expected to trade slightly higher in a 1.1425–1.1470 range intraday.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Faces pressure near 0.5700 in countdown to RBNZ policy
item.description: The NZD/USD pair is down 0.2% to near 0.5690 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The Kiwi pair faces selling pressure as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) underperforms its peers ahead of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s (RBNZ) monetary policy decision on Wednesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Trimmed inflation guides rate outlook – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets discusses how the Federal Reserve’s new task force on inflation frameworks under Chair Warsh may elevate trimmed inflation in policy decisions.

item.title: European Central Bank: Cautious path to further hike – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas analysts assess recent European Central Bank (ECB) communication from Sintra, highlighting Christine Lagarde’s cautious stance and shift toward “framework guidance” in a volatile environment.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Weakness extends against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that USD/CAD has broken out of a large consolidation and extended gains towards 1.4250, with the upper part of the prior range at 1.4130 now acting as key support.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $60.95 per troy ounce, down 1.79% from the $62.06 it cost on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: High bar for hawkish BoJ repricing – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/JPY is consolidating around 162.00 after touching a 40‑year high near 162.84.

item.title: Indian Rupee bounces back as oil prices remain broadly lower
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) in India's afternoon trading hours on Tuesday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index firms as Hormuz tensions boost safe-haven demand
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is holding gains after two successive flat days and trading around 100.90 during the European hours on Tuesday.

item.title: China turns out Gold buyer again
item.description: According to data from the People's Bank of China (PBoC), world’s second-largest economy China increases its Gold reserves again.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Dovish inflation path supports more cuts – ING
item.description: Frantisek Taborsky at ING highlights Hungarian inflation falling to 1.7%, below market and National Bank of Hungary (NBH) forecasts, cementing rate cuts in July and August. Markets price around 150bp of easing and a 4.50% terminal rate, with scope for additional cuts.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: More downside is likely if Oil falls below $67
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trades 1% higher to near $69.40 during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold remains depressed near daily low amid rising US bond yields, USD uptick
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retains intraday negative bias through the early European session on Tuesday, though it holds above the $4,100 mark. Crude oil prices edge higher amid renewed tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, reviving inflationary concerns.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD drifts below $61.00 as markets turn cautious
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) pulled lower from Monday’s peak and is testing levels below $61.00 at the time of writing, paring some of last week’s gains.

item.title: Dow Jones futures defies tech sell-off as capital rotates to value sectors
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain as investors pull profits from volatile tech stocks and rotate capital into safer assets.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside risks grow toward 0.6980 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes AUD/USD rebounded strongly from 0.6923 to 0.6959, with rapidly increasing upward momentum. The bank now sees upside risks toward 0.6970–0.6980 intraday, with supports at 0.6945 and 0.6935.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Loonie constrained near term – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada ’s (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms describe the Canadian Dollar (CAD) as caught between improving domestic growth and a still-challenging external backdrop. USD/CAD recently rose above 1.42, with forecasts easing to 1.33 by Q2 2027.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Resistance at 0.8075 remains in focus as dips find buyers
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades higher for the second consecutive day against the Swiss Franc (CHF). Downdside attempts remain shallow so far, amid a calm market mood, and the immediate trend shows a mild bullish stance, with resistance at the 0.8075 area under pressure.

item.title: Why the New Zealand Dollar may not benefit from expected RBNZ rate hike
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) continues to trade subdued against the US Dollar (USD) as markets brace for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's (RBNZ) upcoming monetary policy decision.

item.title: US Dollar: Benign FX risk score with hawkish fed pricing – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s FX Risk Score note by Chua Han Teng and Daisy Sharma highlights that FX risk has risen modestly in May and June but remains below prior Middle East conflict highs.

item.title: Euro: Le Pen ruling seen as low impact – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING argues that Marine Le Pen’s eligibility ruling matters more for French politics than markets, as investors have largely priced in a National Rally (RN) victory under Le Pen or Bardella with fiscal prudence.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens despite higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD gains ground for the third successive day, trading around 1.4210 during the European hours on Tuesday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) holds ground, which could be attributed to the renewed geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: ECB's Panetta: Strait of Hormuz governance is still uncertain
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker and Governor of the Bank of Italy, Fabio Panetta, said during the European trading session on Tuesday that upside risks to inflation in the Eurozone economy remain intact, as the governance of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint to almost 20% of global

item.title: British Pound: Strong momentum eyeing 1.3410–1.3445 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang highlights a sharp GBP/USD advance to 1.3397 and a firm close at 1.3391. Intraday, Leang sees scope for further gains toward 1.3410, though 1.3445 may stay out of reach.

item.title: Iran’s Foreign Minister Araghchi warns against US threats
item.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has warned through a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, that the deal with United States (US) could be hampered if the nation continues with its threats. “Negotiations on a final deal will not commence if threats continue.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hike seen but path questioned – Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) to raise rates at its July meeting to reinforce its inflation-fighting credentials, which should initially support the New Zealand Dollar (NZD).

item.title: Japanese Yen ticks up above 162.00 US Dollar and eases intervention risks
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) posts minor gains amid a somewhat softer US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The USD/JPY pair has pulled back to session lows just below 162.00 from Monday's highs in the 162.40 area, easing concerns about an immediate intervention by the Japanese authorities.

item.title: Federal Reserve: New communication risks under Warsh – BNY
item.description: BNY Markets’ John Velis and David Tam examine upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes from Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Chair.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Stability above 20-day EMA backs further upside
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) ticks lower to near 1.3380 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday. The GBP/USD pair edges down as the US Dollar gains slightly; however, the Cable is broadly upbeat.
